confidence.rationale: The official site and restaurant-linked Toast catalog independently confirm material scope and allergen-evidence discrepancies. Confidence is high that discrepancies exist, although menu completeness, cross-contact, and complete allergen arrays remain unverifiable.

Reconciliation covers all 52 baseline items: 17 stale_extra/accurately_unavailable, 2 missing_from_source/accurately_unavailable, 12 exact_match/mismatch, 3 normalized_match/accurately_unavailable, 4 normalized_match/mismatch, 8 exact_match/accurately_unavailable, 2 variant_match/mismatch, 1 variant_match/accurately_unavailable, and 3 exact_match/verified.
Identity is verified for Bastille Brasserie & Bar at 606 N Fayette St, Alexandria, Virginia.

The official site exposes separate dinner, dessert, beverage, restaurant-week, and kids surfaces. The dinner page also links three subordinate menus, confirming multi-service and incomplete-scope risk gates.

The current Toast page displays 27 distinct products across dinner and kids sections, including Fried Tomato, Rillettes Trio, Market Soup, Duck, Lamb, Pommes Frites, and Baguette & Butter. This disproves the upstream claim that 21 products represented a complete Toast catalog and confirms count-drift and scope-incomplete discrepancies.

The restaurant expressly warns that not all ingredients are listed and that online menus and items may vary. Consequently, these menus cannot support negative allergen findings, complete allergen arrays, or cross-contact conclusions.

Restaurant-linked descriptions still support narrow positive evidence from explicit or unavoidable identities, including milk from named cheese, crème fraîche, yogurt, or butter; fish from named salmon, trout, or sardine; shellfish from named shrimp or prawns; and egg from a named hard-boiled egg. These positives must not be erased merely because the source is incomplete.
No restaurant-issued allergen matrix or explicit shared-equipment, may-contain, or cross-contact disclosure was found. The cross-contact gate remains unresolved rather than positively confirmed.

The PDF reproducibility risk is real: the current dinner page points to different dinner and monthly-menu PDF URLs than those frozen upstream, and accessible HTML provides no item-level extraction anchors.
rejectedFindings: Rejected any interpretation of an empty allergen array as evidence that an item contains no allergens; the restaurant explicitly states ingredient lists are incomplete.

Rejected Terra's promotion of aioli or dijonnaise to egg and crostini, bread, baguette, or bun to wheat when the allergen-bearing ingredient is not explicitly identified. Those are culinary assumptions rather than unavoidable identities.
Rejected any cross-contact or may-contain conclusion inferred from Toast allergy-request controls or special-request messaging.

Rejected the broad claim that all three frozen PDFs are necessarily obsolete or incapable of supporting current-surface evidence. The official dessert and kids pages still link the same frozen dessert and kids PDF URLs, although their item-level contents could not be independently reproduced here.
Rejected labeling baseline-only items as historical or discontinued solely because they are absent from an incomplete, service-specific Toast catalog.

Rejected treating restaurant-linked vendor authority as grounds to discard explicit positive ingredients. Authority ambiguity limits completeness and negative conclusions but does not erase valid narrow positives.

Sol did not independently reproduce Terra's claim of multiple changing Toast catalog states; however, the currently reopened catalog alone is sufficient to confirm the material 21-product completeness discrepancy.

summary: Adjudicated as discrepancy_found, matching the packet's effectiveOutcome. The decisive discrepancy is the upstream representation of an incomplete 21-product Toast extraction as a complete catalog, compounded by omitted official menu surfaces and unsupported complete allergen arrays. Terra's central scope and evidence-limit findings are confirmed, while its culinary assumptions, broad PDF conclusion, historical-item characterization, and any cross-contact inference are rejected or narrowed.
